questions.question: The emergence of Buddhism and Jainism in the 6th century BCE can be linked to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Criticism of Vedic rituals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **6th century BCE** in ancient India, often called the era of **Second Urbanization**, witnessed a significant socio-religious revolution known as the **Sramana movement**.
 
• The primary cause for the rise of **Buddhism** and **Jainism** was the deep-seated resentment against the **Brahmanical orthodoxy** and the increasingly complex **Vedic rituals**.
 
• The **Later Vedic period** saw the introduction of elaborate **sacrifices (Yajnas)** and **animal slaughter**, which were not only expensive for the common man but also hampered the burgeoning **agrarian economy** that required cattle for plowing.
 
• The **Varna system** had become rigid and hereditary, creating a social hierarchy that granted **Brahmins** supreme status, which was challenged by the **Kshatriyas** and the rising **Vaishya** (merchant) class.
 
• **Gautama Buddha** and **Lord Mahavira** rejected the **infallibility of the Vedas** and the necessity of priestly intervention, advocating for **ethical conduct**, **meditation**, and the principle of **Ahimsa (non-violence)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Transformation**:

 
 
• Contrary to the **decline of agriculture**, this period actually saw a massive expansion in farming due to the widespread use of **iron tools** and **plowshares** in the fertile **Middle Gangetic Valley**.
 
• The **Vaishyas**, who accumulated wealth through **trade and commerce**, supported **Buddhism** and **Jainism** because these religions provided them a higher social status compared to the **Vedic fold**.
 
 
 
• **Political and Cultural Factors**:
 
 
• The **rise of monarchies** and **Mahajanapadas** like **Magadha** provided the political stability necessary for these new ideologies to spread, as many rulers sought to curb the influence of the **priestly class**.
 
• The **Persian influence**, primarily through the **Achaemenid Empire**, was largely restricted to the **North-Western frontiers** and did not trigger the religious reformation occurring in the heartland of India.
 
• Both **Buddhism** and **Jainism** adopted local dialects like **Pali** and **Prakrit**, making their teachings accessible to the masses, unlike **Sanskrit** which was the exclusive domain of the elite.

questions.question: Which factor best explains the low sex ratio observed in northwestern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Female infanticide and socio-cultural bias**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sex ratio** in northwestern India, comprising states like **Haryana**, **Punjab**, and **Rajasthan**, has historically remained lower than the national average due to deep-seated **patriarchal** norms and a strong **son preference**.
 
• **Socio-cultural bias** stems from the perception of sons as economic assets and lineage carriers, while daughters are often viewed as economic liabilities, largely due to the prevalence of the **dowry system** and traditional inheritance customs.
 
• **Female infanticide**, the intentional killing of female infants, and **female foeticide**, the practice of sex-selective abortion, are the primary drivers behind the skewed **child sex ratio** in these regions.
 
• The misuse of medical technologies, such as **ultrasound** and **amniocentesis**, during the late **20th century** allowed for widespread illegal **sex determination**, leading to a sharp decline in female births.
 
• According to the **2011 Census**, the child sex ratio (0−6 years) in **Haryana** was recorded at a low of **834**, and **Punjab** at **846**, significantly below the national average of **919**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male-dominated migration**:

 
 
• While migration to urban industrial hubs like **Ludhiana** or **Gurugram** can affect the adult sex ratio in specific pockets, it does not account for the biological deficit of females at birth seen across the northwestern belt.
 
 
 
• **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act**:
 
 
• Enacted in **1994**, this federal law was designed to prevent **female foeticide** by banning the use of technology for sex selection and regulating prenatal diagnostic centers.
 
 
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)**:
 
 
• Launched in **January 2015**, this flagship government scheme specifically targets districts with a low **child sex ratio** to eliminate gender-biased sex selection and ensure the survival and protection of the girl child.
 
 
 
• **Low fertility rates**:
 
 
• Fertility transition often correlates with higher sex-ratio imbalances in societies with strong son preference, as families use sex-selection to ensure at least one male child within a smaller family size.

questions.question: Which act first allowed budget discussions in the Indian legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Councils Act, 1892**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Councils Act, 1892** was an act of the **British Parliament** that increased the number of additional members in the Central and Provincial legislative councils.
 
• For the first time in **British India**, the act empowered the legislative councils to discuss the **Annual Financial Statement**, commonly referred to as the **Budget**.
 
• Prior to this enactment, the legislative members had no legal right to participate in financial discussions or scrutinize the administrative expenditures of the **British Government**.
 
• It also introduced the provision for members to address questions to the **Executive** on matters of public interest, provided a mandatory six-day notice was given to the government.
 
• Despite these reforms, the act maintained significant limitations; members were strictly prohibited from asking **Supplementary Questions** or **Voting** on the budget.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1861**:

 
 
• It initiated the process of **Decentralization** by restoring legislative powers to the **Bombay** and **Madras Presidencies**.
 
• It introduced the **Portfolio System**, which gave legal recognition to the system introduced by **Lord Canning** in 1859.
 
• The **Viceroy** was empowered to issue **Ordinances** with a life span of six months during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)**:
 
 
• This act further expanded legislative functions, finally allowing members to ask **Supplementary Questions** and move resolutions on the **Budget**.
 
• It introduced **Communal Representation** for Muslims by accepting the concept of a **Separate Electorate**.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms)**:
 
 
• It introduced **Dyarchy** in the provinces, dividing subjects into **Reserved** and **Transferred** lists.
 
• It established a **Bicameral** legislature at the center consisting of an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).

questions.question: What is the one-time fee required to avail the FASTag Annual Pass seen in news in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 3000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)**, in collaboration with the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**, introduced the **FASTag Annual Pass** in **August 2025** to provide a cost-effective solution for frequent highway commuters.
 
• The one-time subscription fee for this pass is set at **Rs. 3000**, which allows private vehicle owners to enjoy unlimited or subsidized travel across a specified network of **National Highways** for a period of **365 days**.
 
• The primary objective of the **Rs. 3000** pass is to reduce the processing time at **Toll Plazas** and eliminate the need for frequent balance top-ups for daily travelers.
 
• This initiative leverages **Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)** technology, ensuring that the toll amount is validated through the centralized **National Electronic Toll Collection (NETC)** system without requiring the vehicle to stop.
 
• The fee structure was finalized after considering the average toll expenditure of a frequent traveler, aiming to promote a digital and cashless economy while optimizing traffic flow on major expressways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of FASTag:**

 
 
• The **FASTag** system was initially launched as a pilot project in **2014** on the Golden Quadrilateral.
 
• It was made mandatory for all M and N category vehicles from **February 15, 2021**, to ensure 100 percent electronic tolling.
 
• The **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)** acts as the central clearing house for all transactions.
 
 
 
• **Technological and Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The system uses **RFID tags** fixed on the vehicle’s windshield, which are scanned by sensors at toll booths.
 
• The implementation has led to a significant reduction in **Fuel Consumption** and **CO₂ emissions** by decreasing the idling time of vehicles at toll gates.
 
• Users receive real-time notifications via **SMS** and can manage their accounts through the **My FASTag App**.

questions.question: Which of the following was the target of Tenth five year plan of India? I. Improvement in Literacy. II. Reduction in infant and maternal mortality rates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007)** was unique as it moved beyond purely economic targets to include specific **monitorable targets** for social and developmental indicators. One of the primary social targets was the **improvement in literacy**, specifically aiming to increase the **literacy rate** to **75 percent** by the end of the plan period in 2007 and reducing the **gender gap** in literacy by **50 percent**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• Health and population control were major pillars of the plan. It set ambitious goals for the **reduction in infant and maternal mortality rates**, specifically targeting a reduction in the **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)** to **45 per 1000** live births and the **Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)** to **2 per 1000** live births by 2007. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tenth Five-Year Plan** was launched under the chairmanship of **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** and focused on achieving a high **GDP growth rate** of **8.0 percent** per annum.

 
 
• **Poverty Reduction:** The plan aimed to reduce the **poverty ratio** by **5 percentage points** by 2007 and by **15 percentage points** by 2012.
 
• **Employment:** It sought to provide gainful and high-quality **employment** to the addition to the labor force during the plan period.
 
• **Environmental Goals:** A target was set to increase **forest and tree cover** to **25 percent** by 2007 and **33 percent** by 2012.
 
• **Basic Amenities:** The plan emphasized providing **potable drinking water** to all villages and cleaning major polluted **rivers**.

questions.question: Tropic of cancer passes through which of the following neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tropic of Cancer** is an imaginary line of latitude located at approximately **23.5° North** of the Equator, marking the northernmost point where the **Sun** can appear directly overhead at noon.
 
• Among the neighboring countries of India, the **Tropic of Cancer** passes through **Bangladesh** and **Myanmar**. It enters **Bangladesh** from the Indian state of **West Bengal** and exits toward the northeastern states of India.
 
• In **Bangladesh**, the line passes through several major divisions, including **Khulna**, **Dhaka**, and **Chittagong**, effectively bisecting the country.
 
• In the Indian context, this line passes through **eight states**: **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• Globally, the **Tropic of Cancer** traverses **16 countries** across three continents, including **Mexico**, **Egypt**, **Saudi Arabia**, **United Arab Emirates**, **Oman**, **China**, and **Taiwan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakistan**:

 
 
• Located to the west of India, **Pakistan** lies entirely to the north of the **Tropic of Cancer**. Its geographic coordinates range approximately between **24° N** and **37° N**, meaning the line does not touch its territory.
 
 
 
• **Nepal**:
 
 
• **Nepal** is a landlocked country situated in the **Himalayas**, between latitudes **26° N** and **30° N**. Consequently, it is located significantly north of the **Tropic of Cancer**.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan**:
 
 
• Positioned between **26.7° N** and **28.3° N** latitude, **Bhutan** is another neighbor that remains north of the **Tropic of Cancer**.
 
 
 
• **Mahi River**:
 
 
• The **Mahi River** is the only river in India that cuts the **Tropic of Cancer** twice, first in **Madhya Pradesh** (flowing north) and then in **Gujarat** (flowing south).

questions.question: Which dance form originates from the Union Territory of Ladakh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jabro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jabro** is a popular and energetic folk dance originating from the **Union Territory of Ladakh**, primarily performed by the **Changpa** nomadic community of the **Changthang** high-altitude plateaus.
 
• The dance is a vital cultural element of the **Losar** festival, which celebrates the **Tibetan New Year**, although it is also performed during various social gatherings and marriage ceremonies.
 
• It is characterized by rhythmic foot-stamping and melodious **Jabro songs**, where male and female performers link hands to form a circle or a long chain.
 
• The musical accompaniment typically features traditional instruments like the **Damman** (kettle drums) and **Surna** (oboe-like instrument), reflecting the unique **Indo-Tibetan** cultural fusion of the **Himalayan** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya**:

 
 
• This is one of the eight **Classical Dances** of India, originating from **Assam**.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the great **Vaishnava** saint and reformer **Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev** as a medium for **Bhakti** (devotion) in the **Sattras** (monasteries).
 
 
 
• **Kacchi Ghodi**:
 
 
• A vibrant folk dance from the **Shekhawati** region of **Rajasthan**, typically performed during weddings and social celebrations.
 
• Dancers wear **dummy horse** costumes around their waists and perform intricate footwork and mock fights, often accompanied by the **Bankia** (brass instrument) and **Dhol**.
 
 
 
• **Kathi**:
 
 
• A traditional stick dance from **West Bengal**, specifically associated with the **Gambhira** folk tradition in the **Malda** district.
 
• The dance is deeply rooted in **Shaivite** rituals and agrarian festivities, involving rhythmic striking of sticks to produce a unique percussive sound.

questions.question: Which traditional sport of Tamil Nadu involves taming a bull as part of the Pongal celebrations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jallikattu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jallikattu** is an ancient and traditional bull-taming sport primarily celebrated in the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The event is a significant highlight of the **Pongal** harvest festival, specifically occurring on **Mattu Pongal**, which is the third day of the four-day festival dedicated to cattle.
 
• The term is derived from the Tamil words **Salli** (coins) and **Kattu** (package), referring to the historical practice of tying a bundle of coins to the **horns** of the bull for the tamer to retrieve.
 
• Historical evidence of the sport dates back to the **Sangam period** (c. 400 BCE − 600 CE), with mentions in ancient literature like **Kalithogai** and **Malaipadukadam** under the name **Eru thazhuvuthal**.
 
• Participants aim to grab the large **hump** of the bull and hang on to it for a predetermined distance or duration to be declared the winner.
 
• Specific native breeds like the **Pulikulam** and **Kangayam** bulls are specially reared for this event, which is most prominent in districts such as **Madurai**, **Theni**, and **Tiruchirappalli**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thang-ta**:

 
 
• Origin: This is an indigenous martial art from **Manipur**.
 
• Description: It involves the use of weapons such as the **Thang** (sword) and **Ta** (spear) and is also known as **Huyen Lallong**.
 
 
 
• **Vallam Kali**:
 
 
• Origin: A traditional event held in the state of **Kerala**.
 
• Description: Known as the **Snake Boat Race**, it is a major event during the harvest festival of **Onam**, with the **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** being the most famous competition.
 
 
 
• **Bihu Naas**:
 
 
• Origin: This is a traditional folk dance from the state of **Assam**.
 
• Description: Performed during the **Bihu** festival, it reflects the agrarian culture and joy of the harvest season through rhythmic steps and traditional music.

questions.question: What is the audible range of sound for human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 Hz to 20000 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **audible range** for human beings is defined as the frequency interval of sound waves that can be detected by the healthy human ear, typically spanning from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Frequency** is the number of sound wave cycles per second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**; sounds within the human audible range stimulate the **auditory nerve** in the **inner ear**.
 
• The upper limit of human hearing, **20,000 Hz** (or **20 kHz**), is often the first frequency range to be affected by age or exposure to loud noises.
 
• Sound travels through air as a **longitudinal wave**, consisting of **compressions** and **rarefactions**, and its pitch is directly related to its frequency within this audible spectrum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasonic Sound**:

 
 
• These are sound waves with frequencies lower than **20 Hz**, which are below the threshold of human hearing.
 
• Large animals such as **elephants** and **whales** communicate over long distances using these low-frequency waves.
 
• Geological events like **earthquakes** and **volcanic eruptions** also generate infrasound.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasonic Sound**:
 
 
• Frequencies exceeding **20,000 Hz** are classified as ultrasonic or **ultrasound**.
 
• Animals such as **bats** and **dolphins** use ultrasound for **echolocation** to navigate and hunt prey in darkness or water.
 
• In technology, ultrasound is utilized in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) for measuring ocean depth and in medical **ultrasonography** for internal imaging.
 
 
 
• **Human Ear Sensitivity**:
 
 
• The human ear is most sensitive to frequencies between **2,000 Hz** and **5,000 Hz**, which is the range where most human speech resides.

questions.question: Where did Usain Bolt set his 100m world record in 2009?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Berlin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legendary Jamaican sprinter **Usain Bolt** established the standing **100m world record** during the **12th IAAF World Championships in Athletics** hosted in **Berlin**, Germany.
 
• On **August 16, 2009**, Bolt completed the sprint in a phenomenal time of **9.58 seconds**, shattering his own previous record of **9.69 seconds**.
 
• The historic event took place at the **Olympiastadion**, where Bolt achieved a top speed of **44.72 km/h** between the **60-meter** and **80-meter** marks of the race.
 
• This performance remains the largest margin of improvement in the **100m world record** since the beginning of **electronic timing** in 1968.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **New York City**:

 
 
• Bolt set his first **100m world record** here on **May 31, 2008**, at the **Icahn Stadium** during the **Reebok Grand Prix**, clocking **9.72 seconds**.
 
 
 
• **Beijing**:
 
 
• At the **2008 Beijing Olympics**, Bolt claimed the **gold medal** and set a world record of **9.69 seconds**, a feat that brought him global recognition as the world's fastest man.
 
 
 
• **Other Records in Berlin**:
 
 
• During the same **2009 World Championships**, Bolt also set the current **200m world record** with a time of **19.19 seconds**.
 
 
 
• **Usain Bolt's Legacy**:
 
 
• Known as the **Lightning Bolt**, he is an **eight-time Olympic gold medalist** and remains the only athlete to win the **100m and 200m titles** at three consecutive **Olympic Games** (2008, 2012, and 2016).

questions.question: In the context of Mega consolidation in public sector banks, the Andhra Bank was amalgamated into ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mega Consolidation** of **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)** was a major structural reform announced by the **Government of India** in **August 2019** to create fewer but globally competitive banks.
 
• This consolidation process officially came into effect on **April 1, 2020**, reducing the number of **PSBs** from **18** to **12**.
 
• As part of this exercise, **Andhra Bank** and **Corporation Bank** were amalgamated into the **Union Bank of India**.
 
• The merger aimed to enhance the **capital base**, improve **operational efficiency**, and increase the **lending capacity** of the merged entity to support large-scale infrastructure projects.
 
• Post-merger, **Union Bank of India** became the **fifth-largest** public sector bank in the country, benefiting from the strong regional presence of **Andhra Bank** in the southern states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other major mergers that occurred during the same **Mega Consolidation** exercise include:

 
 
• **Punjab National Bank**: It served as the anchor bank for the merger of **Oriental Bank of Commerce (OBC)** and **United Bank of India**, becoming the **second-largest** PSB.
 
• **Canara Bank**: This bank absorbed **Syndicate Bank**, resulting in the creation of the **fourth-largest** public sector bank in India.
 
• **Indian Bank**: It was merged with **Allahabad Bank**, significantly expanding its reach in the northern and eastern parts of the country.
 
• **Bank of Baroda**: In a separate merger prior to the mega consolidation, **Vijaya Bank** and **Dena Bank** were merged into **Bank of Baroda** effective from **April 1, 2019**.

questions.question: In Football, there are ____ types of free kicks awarded, depending on the nature of the offence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Law 13** of the **IFAB (International Football Association Board)** Laws of the Game, there are specifically two categories of free kicks awarded for fouls and misconduct: the **Direct Free Kick** and the **Indirect Free Kick**.
 
• A **Direct Free Kick** is awarded when a player commits a physical offence against an opponent in a manner considered by the referee to be careless, reckless, or using excessive force. Examples include **kicking**, **tripping**, **jumping at**, **striking**, or **pushing**. It is also awarded for **handball offences** (excluding the goalkeeper inside their own penalty area).
 
• A **Goal** can be scored directly from a **Direct Free Kick** against the opposing team without the ball touching any other player. If the kick is taken directly into the team’s own goal, a **Corner Kick** is awarded to the opposing team.
 
• An **Indirect Free Kick** is awarded for technical infractions or non-contact offences. Common reasons include **dangerous play**, **impeding the progress of an opponent** without contact, using **offensive language**, or specific **goalkeeper violations** like holding the ball for more than six seconds or handling a deliberate **back-pass** from a teammate.
 
• A **Goal** can only be scored from an **Indirect Free Kick** if the ball touches another player (from either team) before entering the net. If it goes into the goal without a second touch, a **Goal Kick** is awarded.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Referee Signals:**

 
 
• For an **Indirect Free Kick**, the **Referee** signals by raising their arm vertically above the head. This signal is maintained until the kick has been taken and the ball touches another player or goes out of play.
 
• For a **Direct Free Kick**, the referee points their arm in the direction of the attacking side to indicate the kick.
 
 
 
• **Required Distance:**
 
 
• In both types of free kicks, all opponents must be at least **9.15 meters** (or **10 yards**) away from the ball until it is in play, unless they are on their own goal line between the goalposts.
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Penalty Kicks:**
 
 
• If a player commits an offence that would normally result in a **Direct Free Kick** while inside their own **Penalty Area**, the referee awards a **Penalty Kick** instead of a free kick.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding G20?

I. Its summit held annually.

II. India did not host any summit after its inception.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **G20** or **Group of Twenty** is a premier intergovernmental forum for international economic cooperation. Since **2011**, the **G20 Leaders Summit** has been held **annually** under a rotating presidency to address global financial stability and climate change mitigation. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• India held the **G20 Presidency** from **December 1, 2022**, to **November 30, 2023**. India hosted the **18th G20 Summit** in **New Delhi** at the **Bharat Mandapam** Convention Centre on **September 9−10, 2023**. **Hence, statement II is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **G20 Origins and Evolution**:

 
 
• The forum was established in **1999** following the **Asian financial crisis** to bring together Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors.
 
• It was elevated to the level of **Heads of State/Government** in **2008** to address the **Global Financial Crisis**.
 
 
 
• **Structure and Membership**:
 
 
• The G20 consists of **19 countries**, the **European Union**, and the **African Union** (admitted in 2023).
 
• The group operates without a permanent secretariat; instead, it is supported by the **Troika**, representing the previous, current, and upcoming presidencies (e.g., **Indonesia, India, and Brazil** in 2023).
 
 
 
• **New Delhi Summit 2023**:
 
 
• The theme was **Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam**, which translates to **One Earth, One Family, One Future**, derived from the **Maha Upanishad**.
 
• Significant outcomes included the **Global Biofuels Alliance** and the **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)**.

questions.question: What is the rank of China in Energy Transition Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Energy Transition Index (ETI)** is a comprehensive annual report published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** in collaboration with **Accenture**.
 
• In the **Energy Transition Index 2025**, **China** achieved the **12th** rank, showcasing its rapid progress in integrating sustainable energy solutions into its national grid.
 
• The **ETI** benchmarks 120 countries based on their current energy system performance and their **transition readiness** to adopt cleaner energy sources.
 
• **China**'s jump in rankings is attributed to its massive investments in **renewable energy**, specifically leading the world in **solar photovoltaic (PV)** and **onshore wind** capacity.
 
• The report highlights **China**'s success in balancing **energy security** with **environmental sustainability**, despite being one of the world's largest energy consumers.
 
• The country has also made significant strides in the **electric vehicle (EV)** ecosystem, accounting for a dominant share of global **EV battery** production and infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Energy Transition Index** is calculated based on two main dimensions:

 
 
• **System Performance**: Evaluates countries on **Energy Equity** (access and affordability), **Energy Security** (reliability of supply), and **Environmental Sustainability** (decarbonization).
 
• **Transition Readiness**: Measures the enabling environment, including **policy stability**, **capital and investment**, **infrastructure**, and **innovation**.
 
 
 
• Top Performing Countries:
 
 
• **Sweden**, **Denmark**, and **Finland** consistently lead the index due to their long-standing commitment to **carbon neutrality** and advanced **energy efficiency** policies.
 
• **Sweden** has frequently occupied the 1st position, supported by its high share of **hydropower** and **biofuels**.
 
 
 
• Developing nations like **China** and **Brazil** are increasingly narrowing the gap with advanced economies by accelerating the phase-out of **fossil fuels** in favor of **green hydrogen** and **decentralized energy** systems.

questions.question: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) in India, released by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** is a baseline report developed and released by **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India). It serves as a rigorous tool to measure and monitor poverty across multiple dimensions simultaneously.
 
• The index is calculated using the globally accepted methodology developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, adapted to the Indian context.
 
• The primary data source for the National MPI is the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**. The first edition of the index was based on **NFHS-4 (2015-16)**, while subsequent updates utilize **NFHS-5 (2019-21)** to capture changes in poverty levels.
 
• Unlike traditional poverty lines based solely on income or consumption expenditure, the MPI identifies **deprivations** across three equally weighted dimensions: **Health**, **Education**, and **Standard of Living**.
 
• These three dimensions are represented by **12 indicators**, including nutrition, child and adolescent mortality, maternal health, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, and bank accounts.
 
• The index contributes to tracking India's progress toward **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 1.2**, which aims to reduce at least by half the proportion of men, women, and children living in poverty in all its dimensions by **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog**:

 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the **Planning Commission** to serve as a policy think tank that fosters **Cooperative Federalism**.
 
• The Prime Minister of India serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**.
 
 
 
• **NHRC (National Human Rights Commission)**:
 
 
• A statutory body established on **October 12, 1993**, under the **Protection of Human Rights Act**.
 
• Its primary mandate is to protect and promote **human rights** relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity.
 
 
 
• **IDSA (Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses)**:
 
 
• An autonomous research institute under the **Ministry of Defence**, focusing on **national security**, military affairs, and international relations.
